questions: Have you noticed a new or unusual growth, swelling, or hanging tissue at the back of your throat?
Has it been causing pain or irritation?
Have you had any difficulty breathing or a sensation that your throat is closing?
Have you had fever, chills, or feeling generally unwell?
Have you recently had a sore throat, cold, or other infection?
Have you noticed bleeding, pus, or foul-smelling drainage from the area?
Has your voice recently become muffled or noticeably different?
Have you been snoring more than usual or having pauses in breathing during sleep?
Did you recently injure, burn, or undergo a procedure involving your mouth or throat?
Have you ever noticed this appearance before?
Has the appearance changed or enlarged recently?
served: HLA-B51 and Behcet's assessment (pathergy, ophthalmology review)
results: 1. observation of the jerks: rhythmic palatal movements at 2-3 Hz with bilateral acoustic clicks, louder on the right
2. effect of sleep: palatal tremor PERSISTS in sleep - characteristic of palatal tremor rather than true myoclonus
3. MRI brainstem / dentato-rubro-olivary pathway: inflammatory brainstem involvement in the Guillain-Mollaret triangle
4. HLA-B51 and Behcet's assessment (pathergy, ophthalmology review): consistent with Behcet's disease
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Symptomatic palatal tremor due to Behçet disease–associated inflammatory involvement of the Guillain–Mollaret triangle (dentato–rubro–olivary pathway)

Alternative: Essential palatal tremor  
Alternative: Palatal myoclonus  
Alternative: Brainstem inflammatory lesion unrelated to Behçet disease
